questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer obtains a pulsed wave Doppler trace of the LVOT from an apical 5-chamber view. Which description accurately reflects the normal spectral appearance of this waveform?
options: Monophasic, antegrade flow positioned entirely below the baseline
Biphasic, retrograde flow positioned entirely above the baseline
Monophasic, early diastolic flow showing a high velocity peak
Triphasic, turbulent flow displaying complete spectral broadening
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Monophasic, antegrade flow positioned entirely below the baseline as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 3.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  While measuring the peak systolic velocity of the LVOT in a healthy adult, which velocity range should the sonographer expect to record?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies 0.7–1.1 m/s as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 5.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer evaluates a normal trans-mitral flow profile from the apical 4-chamber view. Which combination correctly identifies the timing and direction of the normal E and A waves?
options: Diastolic flow directed toward the transducer, appearing above the baseline
Systolic flow directed toward the transducer, appearing above the baseline
Diastolic flow directed away from the transducer, appearing below the baseline
Systolic flow directed away from the transducer, appearing below the baseline
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Diastolic flow directed toward the transducer, appearing above the baseline as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 7.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is the normal physiological upper velocity limit expected for blood flow passing through a healthy adult mitral valve?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies 1.3 m/s as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 9.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer is optimizing the spectral Doppler profile of the normal aortic valve from an apical 5-chamber view. What is the expected physiological peak velocity range for a normal adult?
options: 4.0 m/s or higher
questions.explanation: The course review identifies 1.0–1.7 m/s as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 11.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is the standard normal velocity range for blood flowing through a healthy adult pulmonic valve during ventricular ejection?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies 0.6–0.9 m/s as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 13.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  During an evaluation of normal pulmonary venous flow, what causes the brief, below-the-baseline velocity wave known as the 'Ar' wave?
options: The closure of the aortic valve leaflets
The rapid drop in pressure inside the chest
Left atrial contraction forcing blood backward toward the pulmonary veins
Rapid ventricular suction pulling blood forward into the ventricle
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Left atrial contraction forcing blood backward toward the pulmonary veins as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 15.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer records normal hepatic vein flow from a subcostal window. Which directional pattern is considered normal during ventricular systole?
options: Continuous, non-fluctuating flow that remains locked at 1.5 m/s
Antegrade flow moving away from the transducer, appearing below the baseline as a large systolic 'S' wave
A brief, isolated spike occurring during the isovolumic contraction phase
Retrograde flow moving toward the transducer, appearing above the baseline as an 'S' wave
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Antegrade flow moving away from the transducer, appearing below the baseline as a large systolic 'S' wave as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 17.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  How does the duration of the normal pulmonary vein atrial reversal wave ('Ar') compare to the duration of the trans-mitral diastolic 'A' wave?
options: The 'Ar' wave maintains a fixed duration, unrelated to the 'A' wave
The normal 'Ar' wave duration is shorter than or equal to the trans-mitral 'A' wave duration
The 'Ar' wave duration is completely independent of ventricular filling dynamics
The normal 'Ar' wave duration is twice as long as the trans-mitral 'A' wave duration
questions.explanation: Normally the pulmonary-vein reversal (Ar) ends before or with the mitral A wave, so Ar duration ≤ A duration. An Ar that outlasts A signals elevated LV end-diastolic pressure. *(Practice review slide 19.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  You hear a sharp, clean 'whip' sound at the very beginning and end of the systolic waveform on the spectral Doppler audio. What is the source of this sound?
options: The physical movement of the valve leaflets opening and closing
An artifact caused by setting the system's wall filter too high
Normal laminar flow passing smoothly through the centre of the valve
High-velocity turbulent blood flow through a narrowed opening
questions.explanation: The course review identifies The physical movement of the valve leaflets opening and closing as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 21.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer captures a normal aortic valve flow profile and notes a clear space underneath the dark outer curve of the systolic waveform. What does this clear window signify?
options: Laminar flow, indicating the red blood cells are moving at a uniform velocity
An artifact caused by raising the spectral Doppler gain control
Signal loss from positioning the transducer perpendicular to the flow
Severe spectral broadening caused by turbulent flow pathways
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Laminar flow, indicating the red blood cells are moving at a uniform velocity as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 23.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer is measuring the velocity time integral (VTI) of the LVOT. What information does the VTI value provide?
options: The global stiffness index of the ventricular myocardium
The distance the blood pool travels through the tract during a single cardiac cycle
The exact time required for the valve leaflets to close completely
The peak instantaneous pressure drop across the valve plane
questions.explanation: The course review identifies The distance the blood pool travels through the tract during a single cardiac cycle as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 25.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is the expected normal velocity range for blood flowing through a healthy adult tricuspid valve during early diastolic filling?

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer checks the colour Doppler profile of a normal mitral valve from an apical 4-chamber view. During early diastole, which colour pattern should appear across the valve plane?

A dark blue flow profile directed back into the left atrium
A mosaic mixture of green and yellow pixels covering the entire chamber
A clean, bright red flow profile directed toward the apex

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Which phase of the cardiac cycle describes the brief period when all four heart valves are closed, occurring immediately after the aortic valve closes and before the mitral valve opens?

Late Diastasis interval
Rapid diastolic Ejection Phase
Isovolumic Contraction Time (IVCT)

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept. Precisely 90 degrees, maximizing lateral resolution
Less than 20 degrees, keeping the angle's cosine close to 1.0

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer captures a normal aortic valve flow profile and notes a clear space underneath the dark outer curve of the systolic waveform. What does this clear window signify?
options: Signal loss from positioning the transducer perpendicular to the flow
Severe spectral broadening caused by turbulent flow pathways
Laminar flow, indicating the red blood cells are moving at a uniform velocity
An artifact caused by raising the spectral Doppler gain control
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Laminar flow, indicating the red blood cells are moving at a uniform velocity as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 23.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer is measuring the velocity time integral (VTI) of the LVOT. What information does the VTI value provide?
options: The peak instantaneous pressure drop across the valve plane
The exact time required for the valve leaflets to close completely
The global stiffness index of the ventricular myocardium
The distance the blood pool travels through the tract during a single cardiac cycle
questions.explanation: The course review identifies The distance the blood pool travels through the tract during a single cardiac cycle as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 25.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is the expected normal velocity range for blood flowing through a healthy adult tricuspid valve during early diastolic filling?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies 0.3–0.7 m/s as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 27.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer checks the colour Doppler profile of a normal mitral valve from an apical 4-chamber view. During early diastole, which colour pattern should appear across the valve plane?
options: A thick black band indicating total signal loss from a high wall filter
A mosaic mixture of green and yellow pixels covering the entire chamber
A dark blue flow profile directed back into the left atrium
A clean, bright red flow profile directed toward the apex
questions.explanation: The course review identifies A clean, bright red flow profile directed toward the apex as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 29.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Which phase of the cardiac cycle describes the brief period when all four heart valves are closed, occurring immediately after the aortic valve closes and before the mitral valve opens?
options: Rapid diastolic Ejection Phase
Late Diastasis interval
Isovolumic Relaxation Time (IVRT)
Isovolumic Contraction Time (IVCT)
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Isovolumic Relaxation Time (IVRT) as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 31.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer measures the hepatic vein reversal ('A') wave and notes it is within the normal range. What is the standard upper limit for a normal adult 'A' wave velocity in the hepatic veins?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies 0.3 m/s as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 33.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  When checking beam alignment for an aortic valve flow profile from an apical 5-chamber window, what is the maximum acceptable intercept angle to avoid significant velocity underestimation?
options: Less than 20 degrees, keeping the angle's cosine close to 1.0
Between 45 and 55 degrees to minimize baseline artifact
Precisely 90 degrees, maximizing lateral resolution
Exactly 60 degrees, using automated angle-correction software
questions.explanation: Keep the beam within ~20° of parallel so cosθ stays ≥ 0.94, holding velocity underestimation under ~6%. *(Practice review slide 35.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  A sonographer records a normal antegrade trans-aortic velocity profile from an apex-down apical 5-chamber view. Where should this waveform appear on the spectral display?
options: Entirely above the zero baseline as a positive frequency shift
Symmetrically duplicated on both sides of the baseline simultaneously
Entirely below the zero baseline as a negative frequency shift
Shifted to the far-right edge of the display grid independent of the baseline
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Entirely below the zero baseline as a negative frequency shift as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 37.)*

questions.stem: A trainee is preparing for a practical echocardiography assessment.  A sonographer obtains a pulsed wave Doppler trace of the LVOT from an apical 5-chamber view. Which description accurately reflects the normal spectral appearance of this waveform?
options: Monophasic, antegrade flow positioned entirely below the baseline
Triphasic, turbulent flow displaying complete spectral broadening
Biphasic, retrograde flow positioned entirely above the baseline
Monophasic, early diastolic flow showing a high velocity peak
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Monophasic, antegrade flow positioned entirely below the baseline as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 3.)*

questions.stem: A trainee is preparing for a practical echocardiography assessment.  While measuring the peak systolic velocity of the LVOT in a healthy adult, which velocity range should the sonographer expect to record?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies 0.7–1.1 m/s as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 5.)*
